guitar.guitaristsText: Eric Clapton / Jeff Beck / Jimmy Page (successive lead guitarists)
guitar.modelsText: Fender Esquire/Telecaster (Page era) / Gibson ES-335 / Fender Strat (Beck era)
guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: The Yardbirds famously had three legendary guitarists pass through in succession (Clapton, Beck, Page), each with documented gear, though no single instrument represents the whole band.
guitar.notes: Notable band for having three iconic guitarists; gear varies by era.

tone.target: 1965 jangly pop-rock with harpsichord, bongos, clean guitar accent
tone.profile: 1965 jangly pop-rock with harpsichord, bongos, clean guitar accent
tone.summary: A pristine signal chain emphasizing compression, chorus, and a clean Fender-style amp setup with minimal reverb to capture the bright, rhythmic jangle of early 60s pop records.
corrections: guitar is rhythmic texture not lead voice

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and maintain a tight signal for jangly pop.
Smooth out dynamics and provide the necessary 'pop' punch for rhythmic strumming.
Keep the tone clean and bright; no grit or overdrive needed.
Simulate the clean, bright sound of a Fender-style combo amp (Gretsch/Fender clue).
Provide a bright, articulate, and compact sound suitable for jangly pop.
Add the characteristic 'jangly' shimmer and width associated with 60s pop production.
Brighten the high end and cut unnecessary low-end mud, enhancing the 'jangly' quality.
Provide a subtle sense of space (mono 60s studio feel) without creating an excessive 'wash'.
blocks.gap: The verdict specifies minimal room, so the mix is kept low.

blocks.purpose: Delay is not required for this specific rhythmic texture.

improvements.summary: Refine cabinet choice for maximum 60s pop clarity.

proposals.reason: Enhance the bright, articulate sound of a small combo amp for 60s pop.
